title: Derive the settled-entry count in RuleCases C-001 instead of pinning '7 settled'
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: C-001 asserts the summary line without a hard-coded settled count: missing
C-001 stays green as later slices append settled entries: missing
C-001 still fails if parity output is wrong, so it keeps its bite: partial
Throwaway build-time probe versus a permanent negative test of C-001's bite: a permanent test survives but adds fixture machinery to a suite no gate runs.
Lifting C-007's inline rule-count expression into a shared function versus duplicating it: sharing is one source but touches a green case.

Adding an architecture rule for a one-file test-bookkeeping fix versus relying on the derived count alone: the rule is the only enforcement anyone will see, given O-005, but it adds one more settled entry.
Keeping 11, 15 and 27 as literals versus deriving all four numbers: literals cost a deliberate hand edit only when the parity tool itself changes.
Names and placement of ExpectedSettled and the rule-count function within RuleCases.ps1.

Case-C007 was not modified and its rule-count expression was not lifted into a shared function, as the O-015 decision directs. The design's 'Fitness rule-count source (shared with C-007)' component is therefore deliberately not built.

O-005 (from the SL-031 reflection) is still open: no engine gate runs tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 or tests/rules/SettledCountProbe.ps1. For now the fitness guard rule is the only enforcement anyone will see. Wiring them into a gate is a process slice of its own.
SettledCountProbe -Shape GuardRule reads the pre-fix RuleCases.ps1 from commit 0647ead17aa99f2aace803624966ca4b1edab65b. If history is ever rewritten, that check fails loudly and needs a new anchor.
The C-007 test command (C-010 here) embeds machine-specific engine paths: %APPDATA%\taad3\venv\Scripts\python.exe and C:\Users\sshub\projets\taad_v3\backend.

Twinned (15), facts (11) and patterns (27) are still pinned in C-001, C-003, C-004 and C-005, and C-008 pins 14 and 15 twinned. That is deliberate per the design, but a slice that adds a twinned entry must hand-edit them.

The SL-053 guard rule's 'because' text in .taad/fitness.yaml says the count must come from 'the Fitness rule count minus the twinned count'. That is still accurate, since the direct count of rules: items equals Fitness's rule count (48 both ways), so it was not hand-edited.
